title: Why impact also needs energy
target: Explain why momentum does not tell the whole impact story.
criteria: Compare momentum and kinetic energy as different quantities.
Identify speed as a squared factor in kinetic energy.
Name where energy can go in an impact.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Two identical pucks move in opposite directions at equal speeds. Compare their kinetic energies and momenta.
options: Equal kinetic energies; opposite momenta.
Both kinetic energies must be negative.
Both momenta are zero individually.
Opposite kinetic energies; equal momenta.
cpa.guide: Kinetic energy uses speed squared; momentum includes velocity direction.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: Object A has mass 2 kg and speed 6 m/s; B has mass 4 kg and speed 3 m/s, in the same direction. Which comparison is correct?
options: Equal momentum and equal kinetic energy.
B has twice A’s energy.
A has twice B’s momentum and half its energy.
Equal momentum; A has twice B’s kinetic energy.
cpa.guide: Both momenta are 12 kg·m/s. K_A = 36 J and K_B = 18 J.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: For the same object, speed rises from 4 to 12 m/s. By what factor does kinetic energy change?
cpa.guide: Speed triples, so its square increases by 9.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A moving sample has kinetic energy 48 J. Its mass is unchanged and speed halves. What is its new kinetic energy?
cpa.guide: Halving speed reduces energy to one-quarter: 48/4 = 12 J.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A ball hits a deformable surface and comes to rest without rebounding. Where can its initial kinetic energy go?
options: It must be destroyed because the ball stopped.
It must all remain translational kinetic energy.
Internal energy, deformation, sound, and other energy transfers.
It must become extra electric charge.
cpa.guide: Stopping removes motion energy but conserves total energy through other forms and transfers.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Two impacts have equal kinetic energy. Why can their damage still differ?
options: Equal energy always guarantees identical damage.
Kinetic energy alone specifies every force and deformation.
Contact area, material response, and energy-transfer pathways can differ.
One impact must violate conservation.
cpa.guide: Energy is relevant but insufficient for a detailed damage prediction.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
